Watch a Bot use its browser and tools, answer with interactive results, and wait for your approval before it sends. Take over when it needs you, and connect the agents you already run.

## Getting started ### On your laptop The easiest way to get started is with the fully self-contained app that runs on your laptop, combining the OpenBot frontend and Docker-based backend in one application. [Mac / Apple silicon](https://downloads.copilotkit.ai/latest/OpenBot-mac-arm64.dmg) · [Mac / Intel](https://downloads.copilotkit.ai/latest/OpenBot-mac-x64.dmg) · [Windows](https://downloads.copilotkit.ai/latest/OpenBot-windows-x64-setup.exe) [Run from source](#run-from-source) ### For your team **OpenBot for Business** brings your agents into one workspace with company sign-in, tool permissions, approvals, and audit. Deploy on your infrastructure or work with our engineers on hosting and customization. [**Get early access to OpenBot for Business →**](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=business&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) · [**Talk to an engineer**](https://open.bot/business) · [**Kubernetes setup**](#deploy-on-kubernetes) ### Web, mobile, and chat [Web](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=web&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) · [iOS](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=ios&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) · [Android](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=android&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) · [Slack](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=slack&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) · [Teams](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=teams&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) ## Your workspace. Your stack.
- **Choose your models.** Use OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, or open models through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, hosted by a provider or on your own infrastructure. Keep your provider relationships and change models as your needs change. - **Bring your agents.** Run built-in Bots in the OpenBot server, or connect your existing agents through AG-UI from any agent execution platform. Agents built with different stacks can work in the same workspace. - **Make it yours.** Use the MIT-licensed template as-is, white-label it, or customize it deeply. AG-UI connects agents, MCP connects tools, and the frontends and backend can evolve independently. - **Govern work across your team.** Company sign-in, roles, tool permissions, approvals, and audit apply across the workspace. Your agents use OpenBot's tools and computers under the same policies. - **Get help deploying it.** CopilotKit's engineers can work with your team to deploy OpenBot, connect your systems, and automate parts of specific jobs. [Connect your agent](#bring-your-own-agent) · [Configure models and tools](docs/configuration.md) · [Explore OpenBot for Business](https://open.bot/business) ## Built on CopilotKit and AG-UI OpenBot is built on [CopilotKit](https://www.copilotkit.ai), which is [used in production by a majority of Fortune 500 companies](https://www.copilotkit.ai/blog/series-a). **Your agent stack.** [AG-UI](https://docs.ag-ui.com/introduction#supported-integrations) has first-class integrations across the major agent frameworks and harnesses, including Anthropic's Claude Agent SDK, Microsoft Agent Framework and Agent Harness, Google ADK, AWS Strands, Oracle Agent Spec, LangChain, Mastra, Pydantic AI, Agno, and CrewAI. Many ship first-party support; [Amazon Bedrock AgentCore supports AG-UI directly](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/runtime-agui.html). **Your execution platform.** Keep your agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Claude Managed Agents, [Google's Agent Platform](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform), LangChain's Managed Deep Agents, [Microsoft Foundry Agent Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/hosted-agents), or your own infrastructure. Connect them to OpenBot through an AG-UI endpoint, using an adapter where needed. Your choice of agent platform stays independent of your workspace. ## Architecture OpenBot has three parts. On your laptop, setup runs the backend and Intelligence for you. For a team, the Helm charts deploy both on Kubernetes in your own infrastructure: `openbot-bundle` installs the two together, and `openbot` installs OpenBot beside an Intelligence that already runs. | Part | What it does | | --- | --- | | **OpenBot frontends** | Mac, Windows, web, iOS, Android, Slack, and Teams connect people to the same workspace. Conversations, interactive results, computer view, and approvals adapt to each surface. [Choose a frontend](#getting-started). | | **OpenBot backend** | Runs the workspace API and built-in Bots, connects external agents and tools, manages Bot computers, and enforces identity, permissions, action policies, and audit. Published as signed images and Helm charts, and reached through [one API](#api). Deploys on Kubernetes with PostgreSQL and persistent storage. | | **CopilotKit Intelligence** | Durable conversations, memory, Automatic Learning, and enterprise governance services. Separately licensed; runs on Kubernetes alongside OpenBot. | OpenBot enforces sign-in, tool permissions, action policies, and audit at its API, alongside Intelligence's platform services. Built-in Bots run in the OpenBot server; your own agents can run alongside OpenBot or on any agent execution platform. Both use AG-UI and can share the same workspace. Computer execution is pluggable: use the default Kubernetes setup or connect a compatible external computer provider. [Architecture details](docs/architecture.md) · [Services and ports](#services-and-ports) · [Kubernetes deployment](#deploy-on-kubernetes) ## Open source, local operation, and licensing **The OpenBot application template is open source under the [MIT license](LICENSE).** You can fork, modify, and white-label it. It uses **CopilotKit Intelligence**, which is separately licensed and can run entirely on your own machine or infrastructure. | Where you run it | CopilotKit Intelligence license | | --- | --- | | **Your laptop, for personal use and experimentation** | Requires a free local Intelligence license. Desktop setup handles this for you. | | **Kubernetes evaluation** | Requires a free Intelligence trial license. [Request a trial](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=business&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access). | | **Kubernetes / production** | Requires a production Intelligence license beyond evaluation. OpenBot for Business includes Intelligence for use with OpenBot. [Plans and pricing](https://open.bot/pricing). | **Fully local is an option.** Run OpenBot, Intelligence, and a compatible model locally. A cloud model or connected online app still sends requests to that service. Initial downloads, account sign-in, and local license renewal need internet access. --- ## Deploy on Kubernetes Deploy OpenBot on **AWS EKS, Azure AKS, Google GKE, or your own Kubernetes cluster**. Each release publishes two Helm charts: | Chart | What it installs | | --- | --- | | **`openbot-bundle`** (`openbot-bundle-0.1.0.tgz` in v1.1.0) | OpenBot and CopilotKit Intelligence together, on one PostgreSQL server. Nobody signs in to Intelligence: the chart makes OpenBot's organization, project and key in it. The quickest way to try OpenBot on a cluster, and the evaluation below. | | **`openbot`** (`openbot-0.3.0.tgz` in v1.1.0) | OpenBot alone, pointed at an Intelligence that already runs, managed or self-hosted: its two addresses in `config.intelligence.apiUrl` and `config.intelligence.gatewayWsUrl`, and a project key. | For a first evaluation, you need a cluster with a **default StorageClass**, `kubectl`, Helm, a **trial or production license**, and a model key. The install requests about 3.15 vCPU while it runs, plus about 0.4 vCPU while its install Jobs run; on EKS that is three t3.large nodes, not two. The commands below use an OpenAI key. For Anthropic, a model router, your own database, or OpenBot against an Intelligence you already run, use the Helm guide that comes with each chart (`helm show readme` on the chart). > **Setting up with an AI assistant?** Give it this README and the Helm guide (`helm show readme` on the chart below). The guide covers cloud-specific values, storage, secrets, sign-in, networking, upgrades, and troubleshooting. Use the evaluation below only through a local port-forward; configure sign-in and TLS before sharing a deployment. 1. **Create `openbot-values.yaml` locally.** Replace the placeholders with your license and model key. Keep this file out of source control. ```yaml openbot: config: singleUser: true secrets: licenseToken: "" modelApiKey: "" ``` 2. **Install** the `openbot-bundle` chart published with the release. This evaluation runs **shared computers**: every Bot runs on one computer, and a command one Bot runs can read another person's files. That suits a proof of concept only, and `openbot.computers.sharedModeAcknowledged=true` says you know it. For people, use sandbox mode instead, which gives each person a computer of their own and is more secure: install the agent-sandbox controller in the cluster and set `openbot.computers.mode=sandbox` (the Helm guide has the command). ```sh helm install openbot https://github.com/CopilotKit/OpenBot/releases/download/v1.1.0/openbot-bundle-0.1.0.tgz \ --namespace openbot --create-namespace \ --values openbot-values.yaml \ --set openbot.computers.sharedModeAcknowledged=true \ --timeout 15m ``` On arm64 nodes, add `--set intelligence.embeddings.enabled=false`. The OpenBot image runs on amd64 and arm64, but the embeddings server Intelligence runs for Memory is amd64 only. Without it, Memory recalls by keyword. From the release after v1.1.2, the chart also installs CopilotKit's management agent into `openbot-system`, which connects a team-licensed install to CopilotKit by default (see [CopilotKit management](#copilotkit-management-on-by-default)). To leave it out, add `--set openbot.management.enabled=false`. 3. **Open your evaluation.** ```sh kubectl -n openbot get pods,jobs kubectl -n openbot port-forward svc/openbot-server 3001:3001 ``` Open . This configuration is single-user: anyone who can reach it is an administrator. Keep the port-forward local. The chart generates every password, key and token both products need, creates both databases, and sets up Intelligence's organization, OpenBot's project and the Learning container. OpenBot's server migrates its own database as it starts and does the scheduled work itself, so there is no migration Job and no CronJob. Automatic Learning uses your model key too. For OpenBot against managed Intelligence, or an Intelligence you already run, install the `openbot` chart instead (`https://github.com/CopilotKit/OpenBot/releases/download/v1.1.0/openbot-0.3.0.tgz`) with `config.intelligence.apiUrl`, `config.intelligence.gatewayWsUrl` and `secrets.intelligenceApiKey`; its guide has the commands. A release of the 0.2 chart that still runs the Intelligence it installed is refused at upgrade to 0.3: keep it on 0.2, or install `openbot-bundle` as a new release in a namespace of its own. For a team deployment, follow the Helm guide (`helm show readme` on the chart) to configure authentication, TLS, your database, secrets, persistent storage, and network policies. For a single-container alternative, see [Deploy it](#deploy-it). ### CopilotKit management, on by default From the release after v1.1.2, both charts install a management agent into the namespace `openbot-system` (`management.enabled`). With a team licence, the OpenBot server connects the install to CopilotKit's management service by itself, with no enrollment step. It never connects on OpenBot Desktop, on the personal edition, on OpenBot Cloud, or without a team licence. - **What it sends.** A heartbeat every minute over mutual TLS: OpenBot's version, chart and image digests, the last database migration, pod readiness counts, and upgrade state. No conversations, messages, files, prompts, names, secrets or logs. - **What it does.** It can restart a workload and write a support bundle to a volume in your cluster, on commands CopilotKit signs. It upgrades nothing until you set managed upgrades up, and then only in a maintenance window, after a verified backup. - **How to turn it off.** Set `management.enabled=false` (`openbot.management.enabled=false`
